title: Idle reserve of agents under bursts and failures

hypothesis.statement: Near saturation the waiting time of a task queue is strongly nonlinear in the number of agents, so a small idle reserve cuts latency under bursts and failures far more than it costs; at low utilization the same reserve buys almost nothing.

predictions.text: Steady load 3.6 (service rate 1 per agent): the simulated mean wait for c = 4, 5 and 6 is within 10% of the Erlang C value (about 1.97, 0.29 and 0.08).
Bursts (load 4.5 during 20% of the time, 3.6 otherwise): one reserve agent (c = 5) cuts the p95 wait of c = 4 by at least 60%, and two (c = 6) by at least 85%.
Low utilization (load 1.8, c = 4, utilization 0.45): the mean-wait reduction from one reserve agent is less than 5% of the reduction obtained at load 3.6 (utilization 0.9).

Stuck agents (each fails at rate 0.002 and recovers after a mean of 20, load 3.6): the p95 wait of c = 4 is at least 2x its value without failures, and one reserve agent brings it below the no-failure c = 4 value.

params.rules: Continuous-time Markov chain simulated event by event: Poisson arrivals, exponential service (rate mu per busy agent), FIFO. Bursts: the arrival rate alternates between calm and burst periods with exponential durations. Failures: each working agent fails at fail_rate and returns after an exponential repair time; a task whose agent fails goes back to the head of the queue. Wait = time from arrival to first start of service; tasks arriving during warm-up are discarded.
